title: Safe, orderly and regular migration
summary: The General Assembly debates how countries can manage migration together: legal pathways, returns, children in detention, sharing responsibility, climate displacement and each State's right to decide.

committee.name: General Assembly: safe, orderly and regular migration (practice)
committee.conference: Practice: safe, orderly and regular migration
committee.notes: A practice draft written for class; not an adopted UN text. Positions are estimates from the linked UN voting records.

topic.name: Safe, orderly and regular migration
topic.notes: Real topic. Positions are estimates taken from the 2018 recorded vote on the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration and the statements made at that meeting.

tags.legal_pathways: Opens more regular routes for work, study and family reunion
tags.returns: Sets rules for returning and readmitting people who have no right to stay
tags.child_detention: Stops children being held in immigration detention
tags.shared_responsibility: Shares responsibility for arrivals through resettlement and funding
tags.climate_displacement: Plans for people forced to move by floods, drought and rising seas
tags.data_borders: Shares migration data and aligns border checks and identity papers
tags.sovereignty: Affirms each State alone decides who may enter and stay

resolution.title: Working together on safe, orderly and regular migration

preambular.text: Guided by the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations,
Recalling the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, which says that all people are born free and equal in dignity and rights,
Recognising that people have always moved between countries to work, to study, to join family and to find safety,
Mindful that every State has a duty to treat all people within its territory with dignity,

operative.text: Urges States to open more regular routes for work, study and family reunion, including for workers in lower-paid jobs;
Calls upon States to cooperate on the return and readmission of their own nationals who have no right to stay, checking each case individually and supporting people to settle back home;
Decides that children should not be held in immigration detention and that community-based care should be used instead;
Encourages States to share responsibility for large numbers of arrivals, by resettling some people and by funding the countries that host the most;
Requests States to plan for people who must leave home because of floods, drought and rising seas, including by offering humanitarian visas;
Encourages States to share migration data and to align border checks and identity papers, with strong rules to protect privacy;
Affirms that each State alone decides who may enter and stay in its territory, and that no international text creates a right to enter any particular country.

cards.text: Urges States to create regular routes for work, study and family reunion with published criteria and fair processing times, and to review them every two years;
Encourages States to consider small trial work and study schemes with partner countries, at a pace each State chooses;
Requests States to use detention of children only as a last resort and for the shortest time, while building community-based care with the aim of ending the practice;
Calls upon States to agree return and readmission arrangements that include individual checks, safe conditions and support to settle back home, paid for by the partners who ask for them;
Encourages States to work with their regional groups on planned relocation and temporary stay for communities affected by floods, drought and rising seas;
Requests States to share anonymised migration statistics only, and to keep personal data and identity records under national law;
Decides that every step in this resolution is voluntary and is carried out in line with each State's own laws and priorities;
Invites States to contribute to a voluntary shared fund that supports host countries, with a public report each year on how the money was spent;

events.title: A regional group meets over lunch
events.body: Delegates from one region compare notes in a side room. Whoever has been working with them most finds a warmer welcome when they speak.
events.teaches: Regional groups often agree a shared line before the formal meeting, so time spent with them pays off.

events.title: New instructions from a capital on sovereignty
events.body: A capital sends fresh instructions to its delegate: it wants the text to state clearly that each State decides who may enter and stay. Other delegations take note.
events.teaches: Delegates act on instructions from their capitals, and those instructions can change in the middle of a negotiation.

events.title: A humanitarian organisation briefs delegates on child care
events.body: A humanitarian organisation briefs delegates on community-based care for children. Several delegations ask how it would work in their own country.
events.teaches: Expert briefings do not decide votes, but they change what delegates think is practical.

events.title: A co-sponsor hesitates over the return wording
events.body: A co-sponsor says it may withdraw unless the wording on returns is clearer. You must spend more effort to keep your group together.
events.teaches: Co-sponsors can leave a draft until the last moment, so holding a group together is ongoing work.

events.title: A revised draft circulates in the room
events.body: The facilitators hand round a revised draft with many small changes. Delegations stop to read it before they will talk about anything else.
events.teaches: Revised drafts reset the conversation, because each delegation must check every change against its instructions.

events.title: An NGO side event on legal pathways
events.body: A non-governmental organisation holds a side event on regular routes for work and study. Delegates who attend come away with ideas they can use in the negotiation.
events.teaches: Side events let delegates hear new ideas away from the pressure of the formal meeting.

author: Claude Sonnet (delegated), 4 Nov 2026; to be checked by B. Gough
